messages.subject: Computing Area with R
parts:
Hi All,
I've been doing a bit of research on this, but am wondering if anyone has already got a good suggestion for computing the area of a raster with R. 
I'd like to split the [attached] image into zones depending on the probability values and calculate the area for each zone as well as the total area of all zones. (Zones represented in the colored map and the other map represents an applied threshold of tolerance)

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Computing Area with R
parts:
Are you using the raster package? I think a combination of the commands `zonal` and `area` from that package would work. My suggested pseudocode below, assuming your image is stored in a raster layer `x`

1. from `x` create a new rasterlayer `z` with each cell entry corresponding to the probability 
2. use raster math on `z` to group the entries into appropriate bins of probability, e.g. z[z < 0.1] =0.1
3. run `area` on `x`, e.g.,
> a <- area(x)
4. use `zonal` to summarize area by probability bin
> zonal(a, z)
